## Findings by module

### 7

- **confirmed** (ch-006.txt): HRW confirms the 11/01/1994 Dallaire telegram was one of dozens of warnings and that Belgium, France and the US were well informed; the Security Council withdrew most troops on 21/04/1994 (matches Carlsson). HRW says a CIA analyst predicted up to half a million deaths in January 1994
- **refined** (ch-005.txt): HRW (March 1999) puts the Tutsi baseline at 657,000 (Seltzer, from the 1991 census, 8.4 per cent of the population), survivors at about 150,000, so about 507,000 killed, roughly 77 per cent: 'at least half a million', about three quarters of the Tutsi. Lower baseline than Reader's 930,000; the toll depends on the baseline [ESTIMATE, CONTESTED]
- **refined** (ch-010.txt): HRW: the Belgians registered everyone as Tutsi, Hutu or Twa in the 1930s, with identity cards; self-declared shares about 15 per cent Tutsi, 84 per cent Hutu, 1 per cent Twa (Twa about 1 per cent before 1994). Tutsi were said to be 17.5 per cent in 1952 and 8.4 per cent in 1991. Check the course's identity-card wording and percentages against this and Reader's
- **extended** (ch-004.txt): HRW records grave RPF violations of humanitarian law in 1994; Gersony (UNHCR) estimated 25,000 to 45,000 killed by the RPF April to August 1994, his report suppressed by the UN in 09/1994; Sendashonga estimated 60,000 to 08/1995. HRW says too little data to confirm. The course should state this alongside the genocide so the account is not one-sided
- **extended** (ch-003.txt): HRW: genocide organised through the state hierarchy (prime minister to prefect to burgomaster); machetes imported to arm every third adult Hutu male; Hutu in the centre and south often refused at first and were coerced; ten Belgian peacekeepers killed and Belgium withdrew; law required ethnic registration
- **extended** (ch-006.txt): HRW on international responsibility: the UN force was authorised at one third the size first recommended; Belgium sent about 400 of 800 requested; 5,000 experienced soldiers could, per Dallaire and military experts, have ended the genocide even in later weeks; the US led the case for full withdrawal; 21/04/1994 Security Council cut the force to a few hundred; the second force landed only after the RPF won. Officials avoided the word genocide and called it 'tribal' or 'chaos'
- **extended** (ch-006.txt): HRW: Operation Turquoise (mid-June 1994) used about 2,500 French troops and saved 15,000 to 17,000 lives, but also aimed to preserve 'territory and legitimacy' for the interim government and let genocidal officials flee; about 500 UN peacekeepers protected about twice that number
- **extended** (ch-010.txt): HRW: Tutsi and Hutu first described status (a person rich in cattle; a follower), not fixed descent; Belgians in the 1920s restricted office to Tutsi, excluded Hutu from higher education, and held the 'Hamitic hypothesis' (Ethiopid, Bantu, Pygmoid); not a deliberate divide-and-rule but racist convictions. The Hutu Revolution: November 1959 violence, several hundred dead, Belgians replaced about half the Tutsi authorities, 80 per cent voted in 09/1961 to end the monarchy; 10,000 fled, then about 20,000 Tutsi killed and over 300,000 fled by 1967
- **extended** (ch-010.txt): HRW on the 1980s-90s run-up: Habyarimana's single-party state (1975), compulsory umuganda labour later turned to killing; coffee was 75 per cent of foreign exchange and fell at the end of the 1980s, then World Bank adjustment; the richest 16 per cent held 43 per cent of land (1991); the 01/10/1990 RPF attack and the staged attack on Kigali of 04/10/1990 with about 13,000 arrested
- **extended** (ch-010.txt): HRW: multi-party politics legal from 06/1991; Interahamwe trained as a militia from 1992; political attacks took about 200 lives in 1992-93; army grew to about 30,000; Habyarimana called the Arusha Accords 'a scrap of paper' on 15/11/1992; a secret army memorandum of 21/09/1992 defined 'the enemy' as Tutsi (quoted at length in HRW), so the 'enemy' category predates 1994
- **note** (ch-005.txt): HRW says a UN expert's 800,000 deaths April to July 1994 included deaths from causes other than genocide, so the UN 800,000 is not a count of genocide victims alone; site tolls vary by a factor of ten (Bisesero 50,000 claimed against just over 5,100 names)

Totals: 1 confirmed, 2 refined, 0 contradicted, 7 extended, 0 absent, 1 note.
